units: <cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Deuteronomy 33:3">Targ. Y. II, Deut. XXXIII, 3</cite>.—
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 60a:4">B. Kam. 60ᵃ</cite> <he>ואם ל׳</he> but if not, opp. <he>אם יש</he>.—
<cite ref="Chullin 24a:4">Ḥull. 24ᵃ</cite> <he>הא ל׳ הכי</he> but without it (if the text did not say so).—
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 10a:12">B. Kam. 10ᵃ</cite> <he>בל׳ איהו</he> without him.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 10b:25">Ib. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>אי ל׳ את</he> but for thee (sitting on it); <he>אי ל׳ אתון בדידי</he> had you not been (sitting on it) with me.

Ib. כחו ל׳ כגופו דמי his force (pressure by leaning) is not to be considered as an action equal to (sitting on it with) his body; a. v. fr.—אלא ל׳ but, must you not admit?, i.e. but to be sure, v. אֶלָּא.
<cite ref="Berakhot 2b:16">Ber. 2ᵇ</cite>; a. v. fr.—<he>מאי ל׳</he> what (does this mean)? Does it not (mean) that &c.

Nidd. 5ᵃ; a. fr.—Esp. (לַוו) לַאו m. (= לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה) a plain prohibitory law, the violation of which, in the absence of any severer punishment indicated in the Scripture, is punished with thirty-nine lashes (v. אַרְבָּעִים, s. v. אַרְבָּעָה).
<cite ref="Menachot 58b:4">Men. 58ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>ל׳ שבכללות</he> an implied prohibition, e. g.

<cite ref="Leviticus 2:11">Lev. II, 11</cite> (where <he>כל</he> implies any mixture of leaven or honey); <cite ref="Exodus 12:9">Ex. XII, 9</cite> (where <he>אַל תאכלו</he> refers to <cite ref="N00003"><he>נָא</he></cite>, to <he>מְבְשָּׁל</he>, and implicitly to any preparation not through the action of fire).

<cite ref="Exodus 12:9">Ib.</cite> <he>לא לַאוֵיה כל׳ וכ׳</he> the prohibition in this case is not a special one for itself as is the prohibition, ‘Thou shalt not muzzle’ (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 25:4">Deut. XXV, 4</cite>, which is preceded by the law regulating corporal punishment); <cite ref="Pesachim 41b:19">Pes. 41ᵇ</cite>.—<he>ל׳ הבא מכלל עשה</he> (v. <cite ref="K00760"><he>כְּלָל</he></cite>) a prohibition derived by implication from a positive command, e. g. the law (<cite ref="Leviticus 1:2">Lev. I, 2</cite>) defining what animals are fit for the altar and indirectly excluding unclean animals.

<cite ref="Zevachim 34a:11">Zeb. 34ᵃ</cite> … <he>ל׳ … לוקין עליו</he> the transgression of an implicit prohibition is punishable with lashes; <cite ref="Zevachim 34a:11">ib.</cite> <he>ל׳ … אין לוקין עליו</he> is not punishable. Pes. l. c. <he>ל׳ הבא מכלל עשה עשה</he> a prohibition derived from a positive command is treated like a positive command (the neglect of which is not indictable); <cite ref="Chullin 81a:1">Ḥull. 81ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.—<he>ל׳ הניתק לעשה</he>, v. <cite ref="N01387"><he>נָתַק</he></cite>.—Pl. <he>לַאוִין</he> (<he>לַווִין</he>).

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 111a:16">B. Mets. 111ᵃ</cite> <he>לעבור עליו בשני ל׳</he> to make the transgressor answerable for two acts.—<he>חייבי ל׳</he> those guilty of transgressing a plain prohibitory law, punishable with lashes, contrad. to <he>חייבי כריתות</he>, <he>ח׳ מיתות</he> (v. <cite ref="H00231"><he>חוּב</he></cite> h.).—
